newsitem.title: USA: Haitai unit indicted for illegal contributions.
newsitem.headline: Haitai unit indicted for illegal contributions.

text.p: U.S. Attorney Nora Manella said Tuesday a federal grand jury indicted Haitai America Inc. on charges relating to illegal contributions in the 1992 election of Rep. Jay Kim, a California Republican.
Haitai America, a unit of an international business operation involving the import and export of food and other commodities, declined to comment.

Kim, the first Korean-American to serve in Congress, was alleged to have recieved illegal donations in his 1992 campaign in southern California's 41st congressional district, according to the U.S. attorney's office.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Stephen Mansfield said the indictment charges Haitai America Inc. with laundering $2,800 in illegal corporate contributions to the Kim campaign by using employee conduits and concealing the illegal contributions on the coporation's books and records.
Haitai America faces a maximum fine of $400,000 if convicted on both counts.
Haitai America is the fifth South Korea-based company to be charged with making illegal contributions to the Kim finance fraud.
Hyundai Motor America, a unit of Hyundai Motor Service Co. Ltd., Korean Air Lines Co., Samsung America Inc. and Daewoo Corp. have previously pleaded guilty.
Criminal fines obtained against these four companies has totalled $1.2 million, the U.S. attorney's office said.
